data: This course provides a critical examination of globalization and its multifaceted impacts across nation-states, analysing the expanding networks that continuously reshape the contemporary world, with particular attention to structural asymmetries between the Global North and Global South. It situates globalization within historical, economic, and cultural contexts while engaging with social movements and practices emerging from transnational flows of capital, people, and ideas. The course is structured into three units. Unit 1 introduces foundational debates and conceptual frameworks in the political economy of globalization, tracing its historical evolution through key readings including Saskia Sassen, Amartya Sen, Anthony Giddens, A.G. Frank, Scholte etc. Unit 2 focuses on Indian society, examining the intersections of culture, religion, and class, drawing on the scholarship of Surinder Jodhka, Sanjay Srivastava, and others. Unit 3 explores international migration and digital media as both outcomes and drivers of globalization, engaging with Arjun Appadurai’s concept of “scapes” alongside the work of Koen Leurs, Karim H. Karim etc  to analyse diasporic formations, cultural flows, and the mediascape in shaping transnational identities and publics. The course concludes with a fieldwork-based research project, enabling participants to apply theoretical frameworks to empirical inquiry and gain hands-on experience in analysing the dynamics of globalization in contemporary contexts.
